description: Chapter summaries the reader shows under a chapter's title, keyed by chapter number, per language. Like section headings they are editorial aids, not translation: written from Open Word Bible's own wording, stating what the chapter is about and nothing more, so every language can say the same thing. They use no reader settings. Every summary is an AI draft until a named reviewer approves it.

1.en: The proverbs of Solomon are given to teach wisdom, and the fear of God is where knowledge begins. A father warns his son not to join sinners, and Wisdom calls out in the streets to those who refuse to listen.

2.en: If the son searches for wisdom like hidden treasure, he will understand the fear of God and be kept from evil men and from the adulterous woman.

3.en: The son is to trust God with his whole heart and not rely on his own insight, to honor God with his wealth and to accept God's discipline. Wisdom is more precious than jewels.

4.en: A father urges his sons to get wisdom above all else and to protect their hearts, for the whole course of life flows out of the heart. The path of the righteous grows brighter, while the way of the wicked is darkness.

5.en: The son is warned against the adulterous woman, whose ways lead to death, and urged to find joy in the wife of his youth.

6.en: The son is warned against rash pledges and laziness, and told to learn from the ant. Seven things God hates are listed, and adultery is shown to be ruinous.

7.en: A young man without sense is led astray by an adulterous woman, going like an ox to the slaughter.

8.en: Wisdom calls out, declaring her worth above silver and gold. She was with God before the world was made, rejoicing in creation, and whoever finds her finds life.

9.en: Wisdom builds her house and invites the simple to her feast, while Folly calls to them from her door; her guests are in the depths of the grave.

10.en: The proverbs of Solomon contrast the wise and the foolish, the righteous and the wicked, the diligent and the lazy, and words that bring life with words that bring ruin.

11.en: The proverbs contrast honesty and deceit, pride and humility, generosity and greed; the generous will prosper.

12.en: The proverbs speak of discipline, truthful lips, kind words and diligent work.

13.en: The proverbs speak of guarding one's words, hope deferred and fulfilled, the company of the wise, and the discipline of children.

14.en: The proverbs contrast the wise and the foolish, warn that a road that looks right can end in death, and teach that the fear of God is a fountain of life.

15.en: A gentle reply calms anger; the proverbs teach that God sees everything and that a cheerful heart and good counsel bring life.

16.en: People make plans, but God directs their steps; pride comes before the fall, and patience is better than strength.

17.en: The proverbs commend peace, faithful friendship and a cheerful heart, and warn against strife and bribes.

18.en: The proverbs warn against isolation, foolish talk and gossip; the name of God is a fortress tower, and the tongue has the power of life and death.

19.en: The proverbs speak of poverty and integrity, of kindness to the poor as a loan to God, and of discipline and God's purpose that will stand.

20.en: The proverbs warn against wine, strife and laziness, and teach that God weighs the heart and that the human spirit is God's lamp.

21.en: God directs the heart of the king, and doing what is right pleases God more than sacrifice; the proverbs warn against pride, laziness and quarrels.

22.en: A good reputation is worth more than great wealth, and children should be started off on the way they should go. The words of the wise begin, warning against robbing the poor.

23.en: The sayings of the wise warn against overeating, chasing wealth and drunkenness, and urge children to listen to their parents.

24.en: The sayings of the wise warn against envying the wicked, urge rescuing those led to death, and describe the field of the lazy.

25.en: More proverbs of Solomon, copied by the officials of Hezekiah, speak of kings, patience and kindness to enemies.

26.en: The proverbs describe the fool, the lazy person, the gossip and the deceiver.

27.en: The proverbs warn against boasting about tomorrow and speak of faithful friends and careful work.

28.en: The proverbs contrast the righteous and the wicked, and teach that whoever confesses sin will find mercy.

29.en: The proverbs speak of correction, justice and the poor, and teach that whoever trusts in God will be safe.

30.en: Agur speaks of the limits of human wisdom and asks for neither poverty nor riches, and lists sets of wonders and warnings.

31.en: King Lemuel's mother teaches him to defend the poor and needy. The book ends with a poem about a capable wife, whose worth is far above jewels and who fears God.
